questions.question: You are waiting in the intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights so other drivers will let you through.
Drive around the back of a car blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If a car hits you from behind, straight wheels keep you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line in the middle. What does this tell you?

options.text: You are on a road with traffic going both directions.
You are on a one-way road.
The road is being repaired.
You must stay to the left of the yellow lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a road with traffic going both directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken line means you can cross it to pass slower traffic when it is safe.

questions.question: You see a steady yellow arrow on a traffic signal. What should you do?

options.text: Merge in the direction the arrow points.
Slow down and stop if you can do so safely.
Turn left after letting oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass.
Go through because you have the right-of-way and oncoming traffic must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: What color are signs that show public recreation areas?

options.text: Orange
Red
Green
Brown

questions.correctAnswerText: Brown
questions.explanation: Brown signs show historical sites, cultural areas, and recreation places. They help you find your way when driving in new areas.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, what is the best way to merge?

options.text: Go slowly and wait for an opening.
Speed up faster than the traffic around you.
Turn on your hazard lights until you are safely on the freeway.
Speed up to match the speed of freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to freeway traffic speed. This lets you blend in smoothly and safely. You must yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: What does an arrow painted on the road mean?

options.text: Drivers in that lane may make the turn shown, if they want to.
Drivers in that lane must make the turn only if traffic lights are not working.
Drivers in that lane must always stop before making the turn shown.
Drivers in that lane must make the turn shown while following all traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers in that lane must make the turn shown while following all traffic signals.
questions.explanation: An arrow on the road tells drivers in that lane what turn to make. Follow all traffic signs and signals before moving in the direction the arrow shows.

questions.question: What color are the lines that separate traffic going in opposite directions?

options.text: Yellow
White
Yellow and white
Yellow, white, and black

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines in the center of the road separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: To check your blind spot before turning left, where should you look?

options.text: Over your right shoulder
At your side mirror
Over your left shoulder
At your rearview mirror

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left shoulder
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot, look over the shoulder on the side you want to move toward.

questions.question: When must you pull over for an emergency vehicle?

options.text: No matter which direction it is coming from
Only if it is behind you
Only if it is coming toward you
None of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter which direction it is coming from
questions.explanation: Pull to the right and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights, whether it is behind you or coming toward you.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." When does the new speed limit start?

options.text: At this sign
At the next speed limit sign
You have time to slow down before the reduced speed zone
Only when the weather is bad

questions.correctAnswerText: At this sign
questions.explanation: "Reduced speed" signs tell you to slow down right away. If a new speed limit is shown on the sign, that limit begins at the sign.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Drive faster.
Drive at the speed limit with caution.
Never drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when roads are wet or icy. Rain, snow, and sleet make roads slippery. You may need to drive slower than the speed limit to stay safe.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight ahead.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill next to a curb, turn your steering wheel away from the curb. If your car rolls, it will hit the curb and stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curves ahead.
Divided highway starts.
Divided highway ends.
Bumps in the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the divided highway is ending ahead.

questions.question: ____ greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity.

options.text: High speeds
Slow speeds
Driving at night
Driving uphill

questions.correctAnswerText: High speeds
questions.explanation: High speeds increase stopping distance and crash severity. The faster you drive, the harder your vehicle hits in a crash.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with opposite traffic, you should:

options.text: Return to your lane when there is enough space between you and the passed vehicle.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right side of the road right away.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to your lane when there is enough space between you and the passed vehicle.
questions.explanation: Return to the right side of the road when you have enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.

questions.question: You approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights. You must:

options.text: Slow down. If you can, move to another lane to stay away from the emergency vehicle.
Drive to the right side and stop.
Keep your speed and stay in your lane.
Speed up to pass the vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down. If you can, move to another lane to stay away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, slow down and move to another lane if you safely can. If you cannot change lanes, slow down and give the vehicle as much space as possible.

questions.question: The most important thing about speed and curves is that you must:

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Your vehicle's momentum may make it hard to turn. Lower speed helps you stay in control.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, you should:

options.text: Let pedestrians cross first.
Speed up as fast as you can.
Back up slowly.
Wait for another driver to signal you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go. However, you must first let pedestrians and other traffic in the intersection finish crossing safely.

questions.question: If two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time:

options.text: The larger vehicle has the right-of-way.
The vehicle on the left has the right-of-way.
The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right. The left vehicle can go when it is safe.

questions.question: For a driver 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.05 percent or higher
0.08 percent or higher
0.02 percent or higher
0.1 percent or higher

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent or higher
questions.explanation: Drivers 21 and older cannot drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The fastest or slowest legal speed you can drive on a road when conditions are dangerous.
The fastest or slowest legal speed you can drive on a road when conditions are ideal.
The recommended speed to drive on a road when conditions are ideal.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest or slowest legal speed you can drive on a road when conditions are ideal.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the fastest or slowest legal speed you can drive on a road when conditions are ideal. You can drive slower than the posted limit, but you cannot drive faster. Drive slower in school zones or work zones. If bad weather or road construction makes the posted speed unsafe, drive slower than the limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Upcoming intersections.
Road construction.
The road ahead curves.
Changes in traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead curves to the right.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent crashes?

options.text: Communicate with other road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do something others do not expect. Communicate with other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians. Use your turn signals when slowing down, stopping, or changing direction. Use your horn when needed.

questions.question: When can you honk your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you have lost control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: It is appropriate to use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. Sound your horn to alert other drivers.

questions.question: When must drivers yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses the street carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
If the pedestrian uses a hand signal to ask oncoming drivers to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses the street carelessly.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in the street. This is true even if the pedestrian is crossing against a red light or being careless.

questions.question: If a green arrow becomes a solid green light, what should you do?

options.text: You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
You may no longer turn and must go straight.
You still have the right-of-way to turn.
You no longer have to turn in the direction the arrow indicated.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you may still turn in that direction. However, you must first let pedestrians and oncoming traffic go.

questions.question: Why should you be cautious when passing a bicycle?

options.text: You are moving faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass the bicycle.
The cyclist may have to swerve into traffic to avoid an object on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may have to swerve into traffic to avoid an object on the road.
questions.explanation: Be cautious when passing a bicycle because the cyclist may suddenly swerve into traffic to avoid an object on the road. Always drive carefully near bicyclists.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a roundabout?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Maintain your speed.
Come to a complete stop.
Decrease your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease your speed.
questions.explanation: Slow down when approaching a roundabout. Roundabouts are designed to be driven at low speeds.

questions.question: What is used on some highways to direct drivers into the proper lanes for turning?

options.text: Flashing red lights
Flashing yellow lights
White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes
questions.explanation: Arrows on the road show which lanes to use for specific purposes, such as going straight or turning.

questions.question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass another car?

options.text: Yes.
No.
If there is no oncoming traffic.
If the vehicle ahead is driving under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: No.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean neither direction of traffic can cross the lines. You can only cross double yellow lines to turn into a driveway or business entrance. You cannot pass over solid yellow lines.
